messages:
maya: anyone else seeing a cluster of quiet socket closes after the console rollout? clients drop with no explicit error and then reconnect twice.
devin: yup seeing it in e2e too. looks like idle window + routing grace interplay. sometimes the resume path triggers a full new request instead of resume.
sam: digging through logs — client shows normal keepalives, then a 204-ish half-close and the proxy starts a reconnect flow. snippet from proxy logs:

```
[2026-03-18T15:22:01Z] conn=abc123 state=idle ping_ms=30000 -> peer_close
[2026-03-18T15:22:01Z] conn=abc123 resume_token=rt:xyz enqueued_reconnect
[2026-03-18T15:22:01Z] router=route-A fallback=route-B start_new_session=true
```

maya: interesting — note the `start_new_session=true` line. that should only be set if resume fails. looks like a race where the resume endpoint times out just after the proxy hands off.

infra-bot: alert: 1839-socket-idle-window spike detected (p95 reconnects up 18% in prod-us-west)

natalie: console telemetry shows users hit the reconnect banner and sometimes see duplicate event-sources (two streams) for ~10s. that correlates with billing dupes in the metering pipeline.

devin: hypothesis: routing.grace_window_ms is 5s by default, but our resume auth handshake can take up to ~6s under load, so proxy gives up and does full session create. then client still retries resume -> duplicate.

console-ux: users are confused by the reconnect UX; can we avoid the visible banner if we can resume silently? current banner triggers on any reconnect attempt and looks like a hard outage.

sam: quick workaround: bump `streaming.resume_timeout_ms` to 8000 and `routing.grace_window_ms` to 8k in canary pool. also add idempotency key to session creation to dedupe billing on server side.

maya: can we also add a telemetry tag to the resume flow so we can tell resume-success vs resumed-after-new-session? need a field in trace: `resume_outcome = {success, fallback_new, auth_fail}`.

devin: done a small query: `sum by(resume_outcome) (increase(stream.resume.attempts[5m]))` shows fallback_new spikes line up with the banner times.

sam: code snippet for new idempotency header we can try:

```http
POST /v1/sessions
Idempotency-Key: session-create-{client_id}-{nonce}
```

natalie: dashboard change request: add a per-route panel showing `resume_outcome` and a small timeseries for `session.create.duplicate` billing events. that'll make postmortems faster.

infra-bot: perf note: setting resume_timeout to 8s increases open connections on the edge by ~3% in the canary group; need to watch overall capacity.

maya: agree — run canary with 5% of traffic to start. also add a runtime flag behind `feature.resume-grace-adjust` so we can flip quickly.

devin: I can push the config change to the canary in 10m. will add a short-lived metric `resume_grace_tweak` so we can rollback if it regresses.

sam: small follow-up: we should harden the console UX to treat a single successful resume as opaque (no banner). banner only for >2 sequential resume failures.

console-ux: love that. reduces noise and avoids scaring users for transient handoffs.

maya: ok plan summary: (1) devin deploys canary config with resume_timeout=8000 & routing.grace_window=8000 behind feature flag; (2) sam adds idempotency header and resume_outcome traces; (3) natalie adds dashboard panels; (4) console-ux tweaks banner rule. test 5% -> 20% -> 100% if metrics look good.

devin: starting canary deploy now. ping here when you see first `resume_outcome=fallback_new` drop.

infra-bot: deployment: canary/streaming-config v2 started by devin at 2026-03-18T15:23:10Z

maya: thx — I'll watch billing dupes and the new metric. if we still see duplicates after the idempotency header, we'll escalate to oncall.

sam: quick note — also add server-side dedupe window of 30s for session-create idempotency keys. cheaper than chasing race across multiple components.

devin: canary healthy for 5m, resume_outcome=fallback_new dropped by ~60% in canary slice. bumping traffic to 20%.

natalie: dashboards updated, added `resume_outcome` panel and `session_create_duplicates` alert (warn at 1/min, critical at 5/min).

maya: rolling to 100% given current signals. will monitor for 30m then close thread.

infra-bot: rollout complete to 100% at 2026-03-18T16:05:12Z; metric `resume_outcome=fallback_new` down 72% compared to baseline.
